milestone.title: v0.1 — First usable release
milestone.description: Definition of done: `mdlinkcheck [PATH]` checks internal links, anchors, and external URLs in a Markdown docs tree, is configurable via `.mdlinkcheck.toml`, is installable from PyPI and usable as a GitHub Action, and has been run against two real, unrelated docs repos with every reported broken link confirmed by hand and no false positives remaining.

epics.title: Epic: Project Setup
epics.body:
Packaging, CI, and the shared test fixture every later epic tests against.

No dependencies. Everything else depends on it, because every other epic's acceptance criteria are tests that need the package importable, `pytest` wired up, and CI running them.

issues.title: Scaffold the Python package
issues.body:
`pyproject.toml`, exact fields:

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "mdlinkcheck"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["markdown-it-py>=3.0", "httpx>=0.27"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8.0", "pytest-asyncio>=0.23", "ruff>=0.6", "build>=1.2", "twine>=5.0"]

[project.scripts]
mdlinkcheck = "mdlinkcheck.cli:main"
```

Package layout:

```
src/mdlinkcheck/
  __init__.py
  __main__.py     # calls cli.main()
  cli.py          # Epic: CLI & Reporting
  links.py        # Link dataclass + extraction (Epic: Link Extraction)
  internal.py     # Epic: Internal Link Checking
  external.py     # Epic: External Link Checking
  config.py       # Epic: Configuration
  report.py       # Epic: CLI & Reporting
tests/
```

`cli.main()` is a stub for now: it parses `--help` and returns exit code 0.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` matches the fields above exactly
- [ ] `pip install -e ".[dev]"` succeeds in a clean Python 3.11 virtualenv
- [ ] `python -m mdlinkcheck --help` and `mdlinkcheck --help` both exit 0
- [ ] Unit test: `tests/test_smoke.py` imports every module in the layout above

issues.title: Add the CI workflow
issues.body:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, triggered on `push` to `main` and on every `pull_request`. One job, matrix `python-version: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]`, running:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
ruff check .
pytest -q
```

Ruff config lives in `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.ruff]` with `line-length = 100` and `select = ["E", "F", "I", "B"]`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Workflow file created with the trigger, matrix, and steps above
- [ ] CI passes on `main` on all three Python versions
- [ ] Verified once: a PR adding a deliberately failing test turns CI red (then close the PR without merging)

issues.title: Build the shared docs fixture
issues.body:
A fixture docs tree under `tests/fixtures/docs/` that the internal-checking and CLI epics run against, plus a manifest of exactly which links in it are broken.

It must contain at least one of each:
- valid relative link to another `.md` file, and one to a missing file
- valid link to a directory, and one to a missing directory
- valid root-absolute link (`/guide/intro.md`), resolved against the fixture root
- valid same-file anchor (`#setup`), and one to a missing heading
- valid cross-file anchor (`other.md#install`), and one to a missing heading
- duplicate headings, so `#faq` and `#faq-1` both exist
- reference-style link, image, and autolink
- a link inside a fenced code block and inside an inline code span (both must be ignored)

`tests/fixtures/docs/expected.json` lists every broken link:

```json
[{"file": "guide/intro.md", "line": 12, "target": "missing.md", "reason": "file not found"}]
```

`reason` is one of `"file not found"` or `"anchor not found"`. External URLs don't appear in the fixture; external checking is tested with mocked HTTP instead.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fixture contains every case listed above
- [ ] `expected.json` lists every broken link in the fixture, and nothing else
- [ ] Unit test: every `file` in `expected.json` exists and its `line` is within that file's length

epics.title: Epic: Link Extraction
epics.body:
Turn a Markdown file into a list of `Link` records with accurate line numbers. Parsing is done with markdown-it-py's token stream, not regexes, so links inside code are excluded for free and CommonMark edge cases are handled by the parser.

Depends on Project Setup (package and fixture). Both checking epics depend on this one, because they consume `Link` records and nothing else.

issues.title: Define the Link record
issues.body:
In `src/mdlinkcheck/links.py`:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Link:
    source: Path          # the .md file the link appears in
    line: int             # 1-based line number in source
    target: str           # the raw href / src, exactly as written
    kind: Literal["inline", "image", "reference", "autolink"]
```

Plus two helper properties: `is_external` (target starts with `http://` or `https://`) and `is_ignored_scheme` (target starts with `mailto:`, `tel:`, or `ftp:`, which are never checked).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Link` defined with exactly the fields above, frozen
- [ ] Unit test: `is_external` and `is_ignored_scheme` against a table of targets including `https://x`, `http://x`, `./a.md`, `#top`, `mailto:a@b.c`, and `HTTPS://X` (scheme match is case-insensitive)

issues.title: Extract inline links and images
issues.body:
`extract_links(path: Path) -> list[Link]` in `links.py`. Parse with `MarkdownIt("commonmark")`, walk inline tokens, and emit a `Link` for every `link_open` (`href` attr) and `image` (`src` attr). The line number is the enclosing block token's `map[0] + 1`; for a paragraph that spans several lines, find the exact line by locating the target string in the paragraph's source lines, falling back to `map[0] + 1`.

Links inside fenced code blocks, indented code blocks, and inline code spans are not links and must not be emitted. markdown-it-py already doesn't produce `link_open` tokens there; the test pins that behavior.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `extract_links()` returns inline links and images with the correct `kind`
- [ ] Unit test: a paragraph spanning three lines with a link on its third line reports that line, not the paragraph's first
- [ ] Unit test: links inside a fenced block, an indented block, and an inline code span are not returned

issues.title: Extract reference-style links and autolinks
issues.body:
Extend `extract_links()`:
- **Reference-style** (`[text][ref]` with `[ref]: target` elsewhere): markdown-it-py resolves these to ordinary `link_open` tokens, so emit them with `kind="reference"`. Distinguish them by checking whether the source text at that position uses `][` or `[ref]` form. The reported line is the line of the *usage*, not the definition, because that's where a reader sees the broken link.
- **Autolinks** (`<https://example.com>`): `link_open` tokens with `markup == "autolink"`; emit with `kind="autolink"`.

An undefined reference (`[text][nope]`) renders as plain text and is not a link; don't report it.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reference-style links and autolinks are returned with the right `kind`
- [ ] Unit test: a reference used on line 3 and defined on line 20 reports line 3
- [ ] Unit test: an undefined reference produces no `Link`

issues.title: Walk a docs tree
issues.body:
`find_markdown_files(root: Path, include: list[str], exclude: list[str]) -> list[Path]` in `links.py`. Uses `Path.glob` for each `include` pattern (default `["**/*.md"]`), drops anything matching an `exclude` pattern via `PurePath.full_match` (Python 3.13) or `fnmatch` on the POSIX relative path (3.11/3.12), and returns a sorted, de-duplicated list so output order is deterministic.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit test: against `tests/fixtures/docs/`, the default include returns every `.md` file, sorted
- [ ] Unit test: an `exclude` of `["drafts/**"]` removes a file under `drafts/` and nothing else
- [ ] Unit test passes on all three CI Python versions (the 3.11/3.12 fallback path is exercised)

epics.title: Epic: Internal Link Checking
epics.body:
Decide whether a non-external link resolves: the file or directory exists, and the anchor (if any) matches a heading in the target file under GitHub's slug rules.

Depends on Link Extraction (it checks `Link` records). Parallel-safe with External Link Checking: the two share only the `Link` type and never call each other, so they can be built at the same time.

issues.title: Generate GitHub-compatible heading slugs
issues.body:
`heading_slugs(path: Path) -> set[str]` in `internal.py`: every anchor GitHub would generate for the headings in a file. Algorithm (matching github-slugger):

1. Take the heading's rendered text (inline markup stripped: `## Use \`foo\`` gives `Use foo`).
2. Lowercase it.
3. Remove every character that isn't a letter, number, space, hyphen, or underscore (Unicode letters are kept).
4. Replace each space with `-` (runs of spaces are *not* collapsed).
5. If the slug was already produced earlier in the same file, append `-1`, `-2`, … in order.

Also include explicit HTML anchors: `<a name="x">` and `<a id="x">` add `x`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `heading_slugs()` implements the five steps above plus HTML anchors
- [ ] Unit test: a table of at least 12 heading-to-slug cases, including punctuation, emoji, inline code, non-ASCII letters, double spaces, and three duplicate headings (`faq`, `faq-1`, `faq-2`)

issues.title: Resolve relative and root-absolute file links
issues.body:
`check_internal(link: Link, root: Path) -> str | None` in `internal.py`. Returns `None` if the link is fine, or a reason string (`"file not found"` / `"anchor not found"`).

Resolution rules:
- Split off `#anchor` and `?query`; URL-decode the path (`my%20file.md` becomes `my file.md`).
- An empty path (`#setup`) means the source file itself.
- A path starting with `/` resolves against `root`; anything else resolves against `link.source.parent`.
- The target may be a file or a directory. A directory is valid if it exists.
- A resolved path outside `root` is reported as `"file not found"` (docs shouldn't link out of the tree they're checked in).

Anchor checking is the next story; this one returns `None` for any link whose file exists.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Resolution follows every rule above
- [ ] Unit test: one case per rule, using `tmp_path`, including a URL-encoded filename and a `../../` path escaping `root`

issues.title: Validate anchors
issues.body:
Extend `check_internal()`: when the link has an `#anchor` and the target is a `.md` file, the anchor must be in `heading_slugs(target)`, otherwise return `"anchor not found"`. Anchors on non-Markdown targets (`diagram.svg#layer`) and on directories are not checked. Cache `heading_slugs()` per path for the run with `functools.lru_cache`, since many links point into the same few files.

Anchor comparison is exact. GitHub slugs are already lowercase, and `#Setup` does **not** match `setup` on GitHub, so it doesn't here either.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Same-file and cross-file anchors are validated as described
- [ ] Unit test: `#setup` passes and `#Setup` fails against a `## Setup` heading
- [ ] Unit test: `heading_slugs` is called once for a file targeted by five links

issues.title: Run internal checks against the fixture
issues.body:
Integration test tying the epic together: extract every link from `tests/fixtures/docs/` with `find_markdown_files()` + `extract_links()`, run `check_internal()` on each non-external, non-ignored-scheme link with `root` set to the fixture directory, and compare the resulting `(file, line, target, reason)` set to `tests/fixtures/docs/expected.json`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Integration test: the set of broken links equals `expected.json` exactly, with nothing missing and nothing extra

epics.title: Epic: External Link Checking
epics.body:
Check `http(s)://` links with real requests: bounded concurrency, each URL checked once, retries for transient failures, and no false positives from sites that rate-limit or reject HEAD. All tests use `httpx.MockTransport`; nothing in this epic's tests touches the network.

Depends on Link Extraction. Parallel-safe with Internal Link Checking (see that epic). P1 rather than P0 because the tool is already useful offline with `--no-external`; internal checking is the core value.

issues.title: Check a single URL
issues.body:
`async check_url(client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str, timeout: float) -> Result` in `external.py`, where:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Result:
    url: str
    status: Literal["ok", "broken", "warning"]
    detail: str   # e.g. "404 Not Found", "timed out after 10s", "429 rate limited"
```

Rules:
- Send `HEAD`, following redirects. If the response is 405 or 501, retry once as `GET` (some servers reject HEAD).
- Final status 2xx or 3xx is `ok`; 404 and 410 are `broken`; 401 and 403 are `warning` (the page may exist behind auth); 429 is `warning` (rate limited, don't guess); any other 4xx is `broken`.
- 5xx, timeouts, and connection errors are `broken` once retries are exhausted (next story).
- Send a `User-Agent: mdlinkcheck/<version>` header.
- Strip the `#fragment` before requesting; fragments on external pages are not checked.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `check_url()` implements every rule above
- [ ] Unit test per rule using `httpx.MockTransport`: 200, 301 to 200, HEAD 405 then GET 200, 404, 410, 401, 403, 429, and a fragment that's stripped from the request

issues.title: Retry transient failures
issues.body:
Inside `check_url()`: on a timeout, connection error, or 5xx, retry up to `retries` times (default 2) with a delay of `0.5 * 2**attempt` seconds, then report `broken` with the last error as `detail`. 4xx responses are never retried.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Retries happen only for timeouts, connection errors, and 5xx
- [ ] Unit test: a transport returning 503, 503, 200 ends `ok` after exactly 3 requests
- [ ] Unit test: a transport that always times out ends `broken` after exactly 3 attempts, with `asyncio.sleep` patched so the test takes no real time
- [ ] Unit test: a 404 is requested exactly once

issues.title: Check many URLs concurrently, once each
issues.body:
`async check_urls(urls: Iterable[str], concurrency: int, timeout: float, retries: int) -> dict[str, Result]` in `external.py`. De-duplicates URLs after stripping fragments, bounds in-flight requests with an `asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)` (default 8), and shares one `AsyncClient` across all requests. A sync wrapper, `run_external_checks(...)`, calls it via `asyncio.run` for the CLI.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit test: three links to the same URL (two with different fragments) produce exactly one request
- [ ] Unit test: with `concurrency=2` and a transport that records the peak number of in-flight requests across 10 URLs, the peak is 2

epics.title: Epic: Configuration
epics.body:
A `.mdlinkcheck.toml` file for per-repo settings, with CLI flags overriding it. Every behavior a repo might need to tune lives here as a value, so the checking code has no hardcoded paths, URLs, or limits beyond documented defaults.

Depends only on Project Setup. The loader produces a plain `Config` object and never imports the checkers, so it's parallel-safe with Link Extraction and both checking epics. CLI & Reporting is where config values are wired into the checks.

issues.title: Load and validate .mdlinkcheck.toml
issues.body:
`load_config(path: Path | None) -> Config` in `config.py`, reading with `tomllib`. File shape, all keys optional, shown with defaults:

```toml
[mdlinkcheck]
root = "."                     # root-absolute links (/x.md) resolve against this, relative to the config file
include = ["**/*.md"]
exclude = []
ignore_urls = []               # regexes; a matching external URL is skipped
ignore_paths = []              # regexes matched against internal link targets
external = true
timeout = 10                   # seconds per request
retries = 2
concurrency = 8
```

`Config` is a frozen dataclass with those fields. Validation raises `ConfigError` with a message naming the offending key for: unknown keys, wrong types, invalid regexes (include the regex error), `timeout <= 0`, `concurrency < 1`, or `retries < 0`. `path=None` returns all defaults.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `load_config()` supports every key above with the listed defaults
- [ ] Unit test: a full file round-trips into the expected `Config`
- [ ] Unit test: one case per validation error, asserting the message names the key
- [ ] Unit test: `root` is resolved relative to the config file's directory, not the working directory

issues.title: Resolve config file and flag precedence
issues.body:
`resolve_config(cli_args) -> Config` in `config.py`. Config file location: `--config FILE` if given (error if it doesn't exist), else `<PATH>/.mdlinkcheck.toml` if present, else defaults. Precedence per field: CLI flag, then config file, then default. The CLI flags that override config are `--no-external`, `--timeout`, and `--concurrency`; list-valued keys (`include`, `exclude`, `ignore_*`) are config-file only.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Discovery and precedence follow the rules above
- [ ] Unit test: a config file with `timeout = 5` plus `--timeout 20` yields 20; without the flag, 5; with no file and no flag, 10
- [ ] Unit test: `--config missing.toml` raises `ConfigError`

epics.title: Epic: CLI & Reporting
epics.body:
The `mdlinkcheck` command: wire config, extraction, and both checkers together, and report results in a form humans, scripts, and GitHub Actions can each use.

Depends on Internal Link Checking, External Link Checking, and Configuration. It calls all three, and its end-to-end tests run them together. It can't be meaningfully tested against stubs, since the point of this epic is the integration.

issues.title: Wire up the CLI and exit codes
issues.body:
`cli.main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`:

```
mdlinkcheck [PATH] [--config FILE] [--no-external] [--timeout SECONDS]
            [--concurrency N] [--format text|json]
```

`PATH` defaults to `.`. Flow: `resolve_config()`, then `find_markdown_files()`, then `extract_links()` per file. Drop ignored-scheme links and anything matching `ignore_urls` / `ignore_paths`, run `check_internal()` on internal links and `run_external_checks()` on external ones (skipped when `external` is false), then report.

Exit codes: `0` nothing broken (warnings allowed), `1` at least one broken link, `2` usage or `ConfigError` (message on stderr, no traceback).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CLI accepts exactly the arguments above and follows the described flow
- [ ] Integration test: `main(["tests/fixtures/docs", "--no-external"])` returns 1, and on a copy of the fixture with every broken link fixed, returns 0
- [ ] Integration test: an invalid config returns 2 and prints the `ConfigError` message to stderr with no traceback
- [ ] Integration test: an external URL matching `ignore_urls` is never requested (mock transport asserts zero calls)

issues.title: Text reporter
issues.body:
`report.text(results) -> str`. One line per problem, sorted by file then line:

```
docs/guide/intro.md:12: broken: missing.md (file not found)
docs/guide/intro.md:30: warning: https://example.com/admin (403 Forbidden)
```

followed by a summary line: `Checked 42 links in 9 files: 2 broken, 1 warning.` Paths are relative to the working directory.

When the environment variable `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is `true`, also print a workflow annotation per problem (`::error file=<path>,line=<n>::broken link <target> (<reason>)`, or `::warning ...` for warnings) so problems show inline on the PR diff.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Output format matches the examples above exactly
- [ ] Unit test: exact expected output for a fixed set of results, including the summary line
- [ ] Unit test: with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` set via `monkeypatch`, annotation lines are emitted; without it, they aren't

issues.title: JSON reporter
issues.body:
`report.json(results) -> str` for `--format json`, a stable machine-readable shape:

```json
{
  "checked": {"links": 42, "files": 9},
  "broken": [{"file": "docs/guide/intro.md", "line": 12, "target": "missing.md", "reason": "file not found"}],
  "warnings": [{"file": "docs/guide/intro.md", "line": 30, "target": "https://example.com/admin", "reason": "403 Forbidden"}]
}
```

Same sort order as the text reporter. No annotations in JSON mode.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `--format json` prints exactly this shape
- [ ] Unit test: output parses with `json.loads` and equals the expected dict for a fixed set of results

epics.title: Epic: Distribution
epics.body:
Make it installable: a PyPI release, a composite GitHub Action, and a README.

Depends on CLI & Reporting. The Action and README both describe the finished command-line interface, and publishing before the interface is settled would ship a version whose flags later change.

issues.title: Publish to PyPI on version tags
issues.body:
`.github/workflows/release.yml`, triggered on tags matching `v*`. Steps: `python -m build`, then `twine check dist/*`, then publish with `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` using **trusted publishing** (no API token stored in the repo). The PyPI project and the trusted-publisher entry (repo, workflow `release.yml`, environment `pypi`) are configured by the maintainer in PyPI's web UI before the first tag; record that step in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

Also add `python -m build && twine check dist/*` as a step in `ci.yml`, so packaging breakage shows up on PRs, not at release time.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `release.yml` created as described, and `ci.yml` builds and checks the package
- [ ] Verified once against TestPyPI: a pre-release tag (for example `v0.1.0rc1`) publishes to TestPyPI, and `pip install -i https://test.pypi.org/simple/ mdlinkcheck==0.1.0rc1` installs a working `mdlinkcheck --help`
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the one-time trusted-publisher setup

issues.title: Composite GitHub Action
issues.body:
`action.yml` at the repo root:

```yaml
name: mdlinkcheck
description: Check Markdown docs for broken links
inputs:
  path:     {description: Docs directory to check, default: "."}
  config:   {description: Path to .mdlinkcheck.toml, default: ""}
  external: {description: Check external URLs, default: "true"}
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with: {python-version: "3.12"}
    - shell: bash
      run: pip install "${{ github.action_path }}"
    - shell: bash
      run: >
        mdlinkcheck "${{ inputs.path }}"
        ${{ inputs.config && format('--config {0}', inputs.config) || '' }}
        ${{ inputs.external == 'false' && '--no-external' || '' }}
```

Installing from `github.action_path` means `uses: <owner>/mdlinkcheck@v0.1.0` runs exactly the code at that tag, with no PyPI dependency. Annotations come from the text reporter's `GITHUB_ACTIONS` support.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `action.yml` created as above
- [ ] A workflow in this repo, `.github/workflows/action-selftest.yml`, runs `uses: ./` against `tests/fixtures/docs` with `external: "false"`, marked `continue-on-error`, and a follow-up step asserts the action step's outcome was `failure` (the fixture has broken links)
- [ ] The same workflow runs `uses: ./` against a fixture copy with no broken links and asserts success

issues.title: Write the README
issues.body:
`README.md` sections, in order: one-paragraph description; install (`pip install mdlinkcheck`); CLI usage with every flag and the exit-code table; the full `.mdlinkcheck.toml` reference (copy the defaults block from the config loader story); GitHub Action usage with a complete workflow example using `uses: <owner>/mdlinkcheck@v0.1.0` (owner left as a placeholder); and what's out of scope (no auto-fix, Markdown only, no caching).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every section above is present
- [ ] Every CLI flag in `mdlinkcheck --help` appears in the README (checked by a unit test that parses both)
- [ ] The README's own links pass `mdlinkcheck README.md --no-external` in CI

release_validation_issue.title: Release validation: run against two real docs repos
release_validation_issue.body:
The ship-it check for v0.1. Do not close until every item below is checked against real runs, not a plan.

The repos used are runtime parameters, not part of this ticket: pick two real, unrelated repositories with a meaningful amount of Markdown documentation (ideally ones you don't maintain, so the docs weren't written with this tool in mind), and record which two you used, with commit SHAs, in this issue's comments.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `mdlinkcheck <docs-dir>` run locally against a checkout of each repo, with external checks on
- [ ] Every reported broken link confirmed broken by hand (opened or resolved manually). Any false positive becomes a bug fixed before release, not an `ignore_*` entry
- [ ] Any remaining noise (for example, links to sites that block bots) handled with a `.mdlinkcheck.toml` in a scratch copy, and the needed config recorded here
- [ ] The GitHub Action run in a workflow on a fork of one of the two repos, producing inline annotations on a PR
- [ ] `pip install mdlinkcheck==0.1.0` from real PyPI, in a clean virtualenv, runs the same check with identical output
